name: Uncle Tom Cobley

intro.text: Tom Pearce, Tom Pearce, lend me your grey mare! All along, down along, out along lee. We're off to Widecombe Fair, and you'll not stop us.

There's Bill Brewer, Jan Stewer, Peter Gurney, Peter Davy, Dan'l Whiddon, Harry Hawke, and old Uncle Tom Cobley and all. And there's my lot, and they've been to every fair since the song was first sung.

win: Well, the old mare's took sick and died, and I've been beaten fair and square. Still be at Widecombe Fair by tea.
after: The song's about seven men and one poor grey mare going to the fair on her back. No wonder she haunts the moor. I'd haunt it and all.
